page.after:
What the differences mean

The Keychron K3 Ultra 8K is not a product Dealectric links to. It is first because its maker rating wins on the figures below. The board we link that wins its own segment is the Lofree Flow Lite 2 84, for a gasket mount with a 2.4 GHz dongle: Lofree states a gasket-mounted build, while Keychron's key specs state tray mount for the K3 HE and K3 Pro and name no mount for the K3 Ultra 8K, K3 Max or K3 Max SE. Dealectric does not test units; every figure here is a maker's or a named reviewer's, read 2026-11-21.

  • Days per charge = rated hours ÷ 8. K3 Ultra 8K: 550 ÷ 8 = 68.8. Flow Lite 2 84: 100 ÷ 8 = 12.5. K3 Max: 73 ÷ 8 = 9.1. Logitech G515 Lightspeed TKL: 36 ÷ 8 = 4.5.
  • Why the K3 Ultra 8K lasts longer: 550 ÷ 73 = 7.5 times the K3 Max's rated hours on a cell 2,600 ÷ 1,550 = 1.68 times the size. The rest is lower draw: 2,600 mAh ÷ 550 h = 4.7 mA against 1,550 mAh ÷ 73 h = 21.2 mA. Keychron credits its ZMK firmware.
  • What the extra hours cost at Keychron on 2026-11-21: $98.99 − $72.49 = $26.50 over the K3 Max for 550 − 73 = 477 more rated hours. The K3 Max SE is $78.74 − $72.49 = $6.25 over the K3 Max for 120 − 73 = 47 more.
  • Margin under the budget: $100.00 − $98.99 = $1.01. Each Keychron price is the listing's first-listed variant. The K3 Max's hot-swappable RGB version and other switch or color options were not priced, so check the variant in the cart.

Where the line was drawn. Every row cost $100.00 or less on 2026-11-21: the maker's US store price for Keychron and Logitech, and the price through our link for Lofree. Lofree's Black Friday Month sale takes 20% off keyboards in the cart with nothing to enter, while the product page keeps the higher price. The Flow Lite 2 84 shows {price:lofree-flow-lite-2-84} on its page and came to {after:lofree-flow-lite-2-84} in the cart on 2026-11-21. Lofree's banner gives no end date. At their page prices the Flow Lite 2 84 and Flow84 are over the line; the Flow Lite84's page price of {price:lofree-flow-lite84} stays under it. Left out for being over the line: the aluminum Lofree Flow 2 84 at {after:lofree-flow-2-84} through our link. Left out with no price: the NuPhy Node75 low-profile, because NuPhy's store returned no price to us on 2026-11-21.

Battery ratings are not measured the same way

The hours in the table are best cases. Keychron's and Lofree's listings say "up to" and give no backlight or connection condition in the text we read. Logitech's spec page gives 36 hours with no condition. Only the Flow Lite84 has a reviewer's split by mode. Julian van der Merwe at Notebookcheck estimated it from the drain per hour:

  • Bluetooth, backlight off: 1% per hour, about 100 h, or 100 ÷ 8 = 12.5 days.
  • Bluetooth, full backlight: 6% per hour, about 16.6 h, or 16.6 ÷ 8 = 2.1 days.
  • 2.4 GHz dongle, full backlight: 10% per hour, about 10 h, or 10 ÷ 8 = 1.25 days.

So the backlight and the dongle can cut a rating to a tenth. Dividing capacity by rated hours shows which ratings assume the lightest use:

  • K3 Ultra 8K: 2,600 ÷ 550 = 4.7 mA.
  • K3 Version 3: 1,550 ÷ 124 = 12.5 mA.
  • K3 Max SE: 1,550 ÷ 120 = 12.9 mA.
  • Flow Lite84: 2,000 ÷ 100 = 20 mA.
  • K3 Max: 1,550 ÷ 73 = 21.2 mA.
  • Logitech G515: 1,500 ÷ 36 = 41.7 mA.
  • Keychron K3 HE ($95.99 at Keychron, a Hall effect board): 2,600 ÷ 55 = 47.3 mA, which is 55 ÷ 8 = 6.9 days.
  • Flow84: 2,000 ÷ 40 = 50 mA.

The NuPhy Node75 low-profile cannot be placed in that list. Notebookcheck reports a claim of up to 1,000 hours for the Node75 with no conditions given and without saying which version it covers. The low-profile version has a 3,000 mAh battery against 4,000 mAh in the full-height one, and Bluetooth runs at 125 Hz.

Remapping also splits these boards. Keychron lists its Launcher web app for macOS, Windows and Linux on every K3 model here. Notebookcheck found the Flow Lite84 remaps only through Lofree Key Mapper, a Windows-only download, and that only Lofree x Kailh low-profile switches fit its sockets.

Not recommended: Keychron K3 Pro

Keychron's store showed the K3 Pro as unavailable on 2026-11-21, listed at $66.49. It has no 2.4 GHz dongle. Keychron states 1,000 Hz wired and 90 Hz wireless over Bluetooth, hot-swap on the RGB version only, and a 1,550 mAh battery with no hours given. The K3 Version 3 costs less at Keychron, is in stock and is rated up to 124 hours. The K3 Max adds the dongle for $72.49.
